How much routine work does AI save? A calculator based on studies

The studies show very different numbers – from just under 3% to over 40%. Instead of a single number, the calculator gives three scenarios, each with its source, in hours and euros for your team.

Serge Zabolotny · 2026-10-27

  • KI
  • Produktivität

The calculator

Enter team size and routine hours and choose your sector – the hourly costs come from the Destatis statistics and can be overwritten. Tool and rollout costs are my own assumptions: please replace them with your own values. Everything is calculated in your browser, no data is sent anywhere.

A model, not a forecast. Basis: 46 working weeks per year; the share saved is applied to your routine hours.

How to read the result

  • Cautious (2.8%): the measured average over all working hours in Denmark. Here it is applied to your routine hours – so the estimate is deliberately very conservative.
  • Typical (14%): productivity gain in the customer service of a real company, measured across more than 5,000 employees.
  • Optimistic (25%): speed gain on tasks that suit AI well (Harvard/BCG experiment).

The studies at a glance

SourceWhat was measuredResult
Brynjolfsson, Li, Raymond (NBER)Customer support, 5,179 agents+14% issues resolved per hour; +34% for novices, minimal effect for experienced agents
Noy & Zhang (Science 2023)Writing tasks, 453 professionalsTime −40%, quality +18%
Dell’Acqua et al. (Harvard/BCG)758 knowledge workers, 18 tasks+12.2% tasks, 25.1% faster; on a task outside the AI frontier 19% fewer correct solutions
Peng et al. (GitHub Copilot)One programming task in an experiment55.8% faster (lab result)
METR (2025)16 experienced developers in their own large projects19% slower with AI – while they felt 20% faster
Humlum & Vestergaard (Dänemark, 2025)25,000 workers, 11 occupationsOn average 2.8% of working time saved, no significant effects on earnings or hours
Destatis (29.04.2026)Labour cost per hour in 2025€45.00 on average (estimate), €27.40 to €69.70 depending on sector

Looking ahead: what these figures could mean for IT careers in 10–20 years is in The world in 10–20 years: three scenarios. An example of AI under human control is AI content with human-in-the-loop.

Limits of the calculation

  • The lab is not everyday work: the high figures come from experiments with selected tasks. In real operations the numbers are much lower.
  • Not everyone benefits equally: novices gain more than experienced people, and on tasks outside AI’s strengths quality drops. Whoever only measures speed overlooks review and correction time.
  • Feeling is not a measurement: in the METR study the developers believed they were faster, but were not. Measure your own tasks before extrapolating.
  • The hourly costs are an average: Destatis extrapolates the 2025 values from the 2020 labour cost survey. They include non-wage labour costs.

What I do with it myself

At PflegeOasis an AI creates the drafts of the guide articles offline, and a human reviews every text before publication. The AI speeds up the work; responsibility stays with the human – which is why review and correction time belong in the calculation. More in the note AI content with human-in-the-loop.
